newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia to privatize state-run bank in November.
newsitem.headline: Colombia to privatize state-run bank in November.

text.p: Colombia hopes to sell off state-run Banco Popular, the country's seventh-largest bank in terms of assets, by late November, the head of the government privatization committee said Thursday.

Francisco Azuero, director of the committee known by its acronym as Fogain, said terms of the public auction of the government's 93 percent stake in Banco Popular would be set within the next few days.
"We hope to have the bank sold by the end of November," he added in a telephone interview.
The government hopes to raise more than $300 million from the sale of the bank, which would be the second-biggest bank privatization in Colombian history, Azuero said.
The government sold its controlling interest in Banco de Colombia, the country's second-biggest bank in terms of assets, in 1994.
Azuero told Reuters the government also hopes to complete plans for the sale of its 61 percent stake in Concasa, Colombia's fifth largest savings and loan or thrift, by next Tuesday.
The actual sale of Concasa should take place before February, he said.
